reference.basis: animated black-and-white bar of unknown real length, not a standard ruler

slow_motion.evidence: no caption, narration or visual indication of slow motion; described only as filmed from the side

subjects.description: small orange rectangular block attached to the bottom of a vertical spring

observation.what_happens: An orange block hangs from a vertical spring and oscillates up and down above a striped bar. The oscillation is already underway at the start and continues to the end with no release or catch seen.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: Position s oscillates with ~0.82 s period around ~65 pixels with amplitude shrinking from ~55 to ~25 pixels, classic damped vertical spring-mass. x is flat noise and y equals s, so s is the 1D motion. Candidates go from ideal SHM to viscous damping to viscous plus quadratic air drag allowed on Earth in air.

critique.finding: The block hangs from a spring pulling toward {s_eq} with wobble speed {omega} while soft air drag {gamma} slowly shrinks each swing.
critique.headline: Spring block wobbles on losing energy slowly
critique.why_it_won: It allows a gentle drag that keeps the swing shrinking just right, while the undamped spring misses wildly and extra quadratic drag adds no help.

headline: A law drawn by public randomness, sealed before the run: a linear spring with viscous damping. Found by Muse Spark’s own law, both constants within 2σ of the drawn value (ω₀ 1.97σ off, damping rate 0.4σ).
finding: The block hangs from a spring pulling toward 68.030 ± 0.014 pixel with wobble speed 7.77422 ± 0.00037 1/s while soft air drag 0.46289 ± 0.00071 1/s slowly shrinks each swing.

eyeball.confidence: low - single stills show only small vertical motion, period and damping inferred from typical table-top spring-mass filmed at 42.9 fps over ~7 s
eyeball.law_in_words: vertical damped harmonic oscillator about gravity-stretched equilibrium: x_ddot + gamma x_dot + omega^2 (x - s_eq_vertical) = 0, with s_eq projected onto side-view track scale

clockCheck.why: Clock not checked: with no ruler in view and no length stated, gravity can’t be measured in metres. A slowed clip would look the same.

truth.note: This clip was rendered from a law drawn by public randomness (drand round 6604798) and sealed before the run: its SHA-256 was committed and pushed in 2752b74, the law revealed in b66261e. Found. The drawn law was a linear spring with viscous damping; Muse Spark's own law won, the referee accepted it, and Muse Wonder was not called. With no ruler found, lengths are in pixels; true values in pixels use the render's own scale.
